newsitem.title: INDIA: India Essar JV commissions steel firm in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: India Essar JV commissions steel firm in Indonesia.

text.p: India's private Essar Group said on Monday its Indonesian joint venture PT Essar Dhananjaya commissioned a plant to manufacture 200,000 tonnes of cold-rolled steel (CR) coils per annum.
The $90 million joint venture will supply the Indonesian market, it said in a statement.
The plant was formally inaugurated by T. Ariwibowo, Indonesia's minister for trade and industries, it said.
PT Essar Dhananjaya is a joint venture between Essar and Indonesia's Garama Group.
"While the plant is equipped to manufacture a wide range of CR sizes, the accent will be on import substitution of thinner gauges, mainly in 0.18-0.55 mm thickness," Essar said.
The Indonesian plant will import its raw material hot rolled (HR) coils from Essar Steel Ltd 's steel complex at Hazira on India's western coast.
"Market studies estimate the supply-demand gap for CR coils in Indonesia at more than 550,000 tonnes, even after accounting for the planned expansion of domestic capacities," Essar said.
With annual demand for CR coils growing at 8.0 percent and to take advantage of existing demand, the group plans to double the capacity of the Indonesian unit, the statement said.
The investment in the next phase of expansion is estimated at $45.0 million, it said. It did not say what the capacity would be after expansion or when it would be completed.
Several Indian and foreign securities firms have a sell recommendation on shares of Essar Steel which stabilised production at its HR unit after delay and a cost over-run.
